labels.label: prop:Cauchy_pgcd
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. No statement that existed at AUDIT-1 changed. In SubExtensionAbstract.lean the Lean diff is two pure insertions: l.776-1103 (base_equivalent_bigSub and the 'stronger witness' section) and l.1122-1136 (cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm). The other hunks are docstrings: l.33-43, 58-70 and 1107-1114. CauchyPgcdAbstract is untouched, and `example : CauchyPgcdAbstract.{u} := @Causal.cauchy_pgcd.{u}` still typechecks. I checked the new mathematics independently, in five steps. (1) wideCausality and far2Causality are `Causality ℝ` terms; every field of Precausality and Causality is kernel-checked. The numbers are right: wide = C₀ ∨ (1 ≤ y-x ≤ 4·dens U x y); far2 = C₀ ∨ (y-x ≥ 2). IsMid gives C₀ ⊆ D ⊆ C₁, and D ⊆ C₀ on open sets of diameter < 1. Both instances hold (wide's extra pairs have y-x ≥ 1, far2's have y-x ≥ 2 ≥ 1). (2) midSub hD is a CommonSubExtension in the library's sense. Its fields are IsCauchyEmbedding C₀ D id and IsCauchyEmbedding D C₁ id, with GH from le_top_iff (≤ on ⊤ is the order of ℝ), Cauchy surface {0} via causalCurveIn_iff_timelike, and the local isomorphism on ]x-½, x+½[ from le_small. comm₁ and comm₂ hold by rfl. The setting's hypotheses are those of not_cauchyPgcdAbstract: ConnectedSpace ℝ, T2Space ℝ, isCauchyEmbedding_dens_big twice, and bigCausality_isRigid (the library's IsRigid, checked in AUDIT-1). (3) midSub_isMaximal is the library's IsMaximal, genuinely proved. From Y.b ∘ f = id, f is injective, and f (Y.b y) = y follows from the injectivity of Y.b. (4) not_isMorphism_wide_far2 and not_isMorphism_far2_wide quantify over every f. A morphism must be id (b = id), and id is not an IsEMorphism either way. First, 0 ≤ 3/2 in W = ]-¼,¼[ ∪ ]11/10,8/5[ holds for C' (dens ≥ 2/5, so 4·dens ≥ 8/5 ≥ 3/2) and fails for C'' (dens ≤ 13/20 < 3/4, and 3/2 < 2). Second, 0 ≤ 3 in ]-¼,¼[ ∪ ]11/4,13/4[ holds for C'' and fails for C' (dens ≤ ½, so 4·dens ≤ 2 < 3). The arithmetic is right and the theorems say what they claim. (5) The conclusion 'no reading of equivalent needing a morphism in at least one direction relates them' follows. A probe proved ¬ of the abstract Prop with uniqueness weakened to '(∃ f, X.IsMorphism Y f) ∨ (∃ g, Y.IsMorphism X g)', standard axioms. But 'any/every reading' overclaims (minor finding 1). The equivalence relation generated by Equivalent relates the two sub-extensions through the base. Non-locality is in scope: the data C₀ = dens and C₁ = C₂ = big are proved not absolutely minimal (not_absolutelyMinimalOn_witness). The new carriers wide and far2 are not absolutely minimal either. This is not stated in the file, but it is a one-liner, `not_absolutelyMinimalOn_of_le_gapSet (h.le_of_dens densCausality_le_gapSet)`, kernel-checked in the probe. The SCOPE and the REPORT scope the refutation to non-local causalities, say that sufficiency of absolute minimality is open, and say that absolute minimality is not a gluing axiom, as kb/0014 and kb/0019 require. kb/0030 is not engaged: no relation used is non-closed on ⊤, where all four causalities have ≤ equal to the order of ℝ. AUDIT-1 finding 1 is fixed: base_equivalent_bigSub is stated and proved, and the module 'What is proved' and SCOPE disclose the directional dependence. So do the not_cauchyPgcdAbstract docstring and REPORT findings[1](a). The conclusion is reworded to 'fails without a locality hypothesis; whether absolute minimality suffices is open'. AUDIT-1 finding 2 is fixed: findings[0] ends 'The recorded paper_findings stay', and the notes give the suggested addition.

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/CBG/SubExtensionAbstract.lean:1123 (heading of the cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm docstring); scaffold/CausalScaffold/CBG/ETTSubExtension.lean:76 (SCOPE); REPORT prop:Cauchy_pgcd findings[1] ('(b) ... refutes it under any reading of equivalent') and hypotheses[4].note ('any reading of equivalent'); kb_proposals[2]
findings.what: The stronger witness refutes every reading that asks for a morphism between the two maximal sub-extensions: the directional one, the one-step symmetric one, and isomorphism. A probe refuted even '(∃ f, X → Y morphism) ∨ (∃ g, Y → X morphism)'. It does NOT refute 'any reading'. Under the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms, the two ARE equivalent, through the base. id : base → midSub hD is a bijective morphism for both D (⟨hD.isEMorphism_dens, rfl, rfl⟩). More generally, in this setting base.Equivalent Y holds for EVERY common sub-extension Y, via Y.a: Y.b ∘ Y.a = id forces Y.a to be bijective. A probe kernel-checked this, and also Relation.EqvGen (·.Equivalent ·) (midSub wideCausality_isMid) (midSub far2Causality_isMid), with standard axioms. So no witness with i₁ bijective can refute the generated reading. That reading is a natural repair, because abstractly the one-step symmetric 'equivalent' is not transitive, and this very witness shows it: base ~ C', base ~ C'', C' ≁ C''. So 'unique up to equivalence' is ill-posed in the abstract setting until a reading is fixed. In the paper's setting all readings coincide (isMor_inv). The author-facing sentence '(b) refutes it under any reading' is false for that reading. kb_proposals[2] ('a refutation ... should exhibit sub-extensions with no morphism either way') states a necessary condition, not a sufficient one.
findings.fix: Replace 'any/every reading of "equivalent"' with 'every reading that asks for a morphism between the two (directional, symmetric, isomorphism)' in the docstring heading at l.1123, in ETTSubExtension l.76, in REPORT findings[1](b) and in hypotheses[4].note. Add to the SubExtensionAbstract SCOPE and to the REPORT: 'Not refuted: the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms. Here the base maps bijectively onto every common sub-extension, so X ← base → Y. Abstractly the symmetric relation is not transitive (this witness), so the statement needs its reading fixed. Whether the generated reading is refutable (necessarily with i₁ not bijective) is open.' Optionally state the zigzag as a theorem. It is a four-line proof by Y.a, Y.comm₁, Y.comm₂, Y.ha and Y.hb.injective.

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/CBG/SubExtensionAbstract.lean:1055-1056 and 1081-1082 (docstrings of not_isMorphism_wide_far2 and not_isMorphism_far2_wide); REPORT notes ('No existing statement or proof changed. retiring it in favour of ...')
findings.what: These are wording defects; the proofs are right. (a) The far2→wide docstring says 'U fills only ½ of ]0, 3]'. The actual measure is |W ∩ ]0,3]| ≤ ½, which is a sixth of the interval. 'Fills ½ of' reads as a fraction, and a half would satisfy C' (which asks for a quarter), so the gloss contradicts the definition it explains. The wide→far2 gloss 'fills 2/5 ≥ ¼ of ]0, 3/2] past 1' mixes a length (2/5) with a fraction (¼). The inequality used is 2/5 ≥ 3/8 = (3/2)/4. (b) In the REPORT notes, the fix-round sentence was spliced in front of 'retiring it in favour of the Prop and its refutation ...'. That sentence now starts in lower case, and its 'it' (the scaffold's sorried cauchy_pgcd) has lost its antecedent.
findings.fix: (a) Write '|W ∩ ]0,3]| ≤ ½ < ¾, so U fills a sixth, not a quarter' and '|W ∩ ]11/10, 3/2]| = 2/5 ≥ 3/8 = ¼ · 3/2'. (b) Write 'Retiring CausalScaffold.SubExtension.cauchy_pgcd in favour of the Prop and its refutation ...'.
